entry.title: Doom GPU Flame Graphs
entry.summary:
Imagine halving the resource costs of AI and what that could mean for the planet and the industry -- based on extreme estimates such savings could reduce the total US power usage by over 10% by 2030 1 . At Intel we've been creating a new analyzer tool to help reduce AI costs called AI Flame Graphs : a visualization that shows an AI accelerator or GPU hardware profile along with the full software stack, based on my CPU flame graphs . Our first version is available to customers in the Intel Tiber AI Cloud as a preview for the Intel Data Center GPU Max Series (previously called Ponte Vecchio).

Source: Brendan Gregg (Systems Performance & eBPF) · Tags: #kernel-os #performance #compilers #combinatorics

entry.title: How to get an attractive model. We give a fourth-order Calabi-Yau differential operator, which seems to have been missed by earlier tabulations.
entry.summary:
We give a fourth-order Calabi-Yau differential operator, which seems to have been missed by earlier tabulations. We draw attention to this operator because of its clear geometric interpretation and evidence that it possesses a rank-two attractor, conjecturally giving a new example of a Calabi-Yau threefold with modularity properties analogous to those of an elliptic curve over $\mathbb{Q}$.

Source: arXiv Mathematics (NT, CO, AG, LO, AT, GR) · Tags: #number-theory #combinatorics #high-energy #algebra-geometry

entry.title: Information-theoretic entropy imaging of quantum matter
entry.summary:
Phase transitions can generate intricate spatial organization invisible to spatially averaged probes, yet quantitative measures of this organization remain limited. Here we develop "entropy imaging," an information-theoretic technique that harnesses lossless compression to quantify spatial complexity, predictability, and order in quantum materials. Using this approach, emergent spatial textures can be imaged and converted into an experimentally-accessible observable: the computable information density (CID), a compression-based measure of information complexity that approaches the Shannon entropy rate in the large-system limit.

Source: arXiv Quantum & Condensed Matter (quant-ph, cond-mat) · Tags: #quantum-computing #condensed-matter #materials-science #combinatorics

entry.title: flodl-bio: First Rust data, transformers and model layer for entire deep learning on biological sequences
entry.summary:
Python ecosystem dominates the deep learning framework. flodl-bio is a Rust crate that extends flodl, a libtorch-backed deep-learning framework, with deep learning on biological sequences. To our knowledge, flodl-bio is the first Rust crate that provides a comprehensive and practical deep learning for the biological applications, which includes the alphabet-aware sequence encoding, including one-hot and k-mer representations, padded sequences, and channels-first batches.

Source: bioRxiv Bioinformatics Preprints · Tags: #bioinformatics #genomics-proteins #rust #combinatorics

entry.title: Practical, Round-Optimal Lattice-Based Blind Signatures. Blind signatures are a fundamental cryptographic primitive with numerous practical applications.
entry.summary:
Blind signatures are a fundamental cryptographic primitive with numerous practical applications. While there exist many practical blind signatures from number-theoretic assumptions, the situation is far less satisfactory from post-quantum assumptions. In this work, we provide the first overall practical, lattice-based blind signature, supporting an unbounded number of signature queries and additionally enjoying optimal round complexity.

Source: IACR Cryptology ePrint Archive · Tags: #cryptography #zkp #post-quantum #combinatorics

entry.title: On Lifting AGM Security to the AGM with Oblivious Sampling. The Algebraic Group Model (AGM) is widely used to prove the security of cryptographic schemes involving groups and pairings.
entry.summary:
The Algebraic Group Model (AGM) is widely used to prove the security of cryptographic schemes involving groups and pairings. It requires adversaries to explain how their output group elements are obtained from the elements they have received. The AGM with Oblivious Sampling (AGMOS), introduced by Lipmaa, Parisella, and Siim (TCC 2023), additionally allows adversaries to sample group elements without learning their discrete logarithms.

Source: IACR Cryptology ePrint Archive · Tags: #cryptography #zkp #logic #combinatorics

entry.title: Insuring Landlords -- by Thomas Bézy, Antoine B. Levy, Timothy McQuade
entry.summary:
This paper shows that insuring landlords against non-payment risk can improve housing access and upward geographic mobility for fragile tenants. We study Visale, a large-scale publicly funded rent guarantee insurance policy in France, free for eligible tenants and landlords. Using administrative household and claim payout data and quasi-experimental eligibility variation by exact age, we show the guarantee increased access to private-sector rental housing, especially for immigrants, newly formed households, and low-income renters.

Source: NBER Working Papers (National Bureau of Economic Research) · Tags: #macroeconomics #econometrics #combinatorics
